sections.title: Joash's Reign Begins
observations: Joash becomes king at a young age, illustrating God's providence in preserving the Davidic line despite the threats against it.
His reign is marked by a commitment to the worship of Yahweh, influenced by the high priest Jehoiada, which reflects the importance of godly leadership in guiding a nation.

sections.title: Restoration of the Temple
observations: Joash initiates a significant project to repair the temple, demonstrating the importance of the house of God in the life of Israel.
The collection of funds for the temple repairs shows the communal responsibility of the people in maintaining their worship space.

sections.title: Jehoiada's Influence and Death
observations: Jehoiada's role as a mentor to Joash is crucial; his guidance leads to a period of spiritual renewal.
The chapter highlights the dangers of leadership without godly counsel, as Joash's faithfulness wanes after Jehoiada's death.

sections.title: Apostasy and Consequences
observations: After Jehoiada's death, Joash turns away from Yahweh, showing how quickly a leader can lead a nation astray.
The consequences of apostasy are severe, as the people face judgment and oppression from surrounding nations.

importantVerses.commentary: Joash did what was right in the eyes of the Lord all the years Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
Let them give it to those who do the work, who oversee the repairs of the temple.
They abandoned the temple of the Lord, the God of their ancestors, and worshiped Asherah poles and idols.

questions: What does Joash's early faithfulness teach us about the influence of godly mentors?
How can the church today learn from the importance of maintaining the house of God?
What are the implications of turning away from God after a period of faithfulness?
